summary.business_type: Service business — paid intermediary booking US visa (AIS/CGI) interview appointments
top_findings: 7 of 14 sitemap URLs are 'URL is unknown to Google' — never crawled, never indexed. These include every commercial /services/ page, /about/, and all 3 policy pages. The site's entire conversion path is invisible to Google while only blog content ranks.

Cause is crawl demand plus a stale sitemap, NOT internal linking: /services/ has 8 homepage links yet zero referring URLs recorded, while /blog/ is indexed with no nav link at all. Google's sitemap copy was last processed 2026-06-23 with 10 URLs; the live file has 14.

/services/ and the homepage link to 3 location pages that return 404 AND are robots.txt-Disallow'd (dubai, uae, australia). The Disallow prevents Google from ever observing the 404, so the URLs cannot be cleanly dropped.
Zero social proof sitewide in a scam-heavy YMYL niche — homepage HTML literally contains '<!-- Testimonial section removed -->'. /terms/ promises registered company details it never provides.

Link acquisition is the binding constraint: bottom of Common Crawl authority distribution, no discoverable referring domains, and the targeted head terms are owned by the official government booking portal (ais.usvisa-info.com) and travel.state.gov.
quick_wins: Resubmit sitemap.xml in GSC (Google's copy is 7 weeks stale, 10 URLs vs live 14)
Request Indexing for the 7 unknown URLs via GSC URL Inspection
Fix live production schema placeholder: Organization.sameAs contains literal 'https://t.me/YourTelegramChannel' (2 minutes)
Fix favicon case bug: brand-logo-real.PNG is 200, .png is 404 on case-sensitive Vercel — breaks 8 pages (5 minutes)
Move the existing 'not affiliated with the U.S. Government' disclaimer from the footer (~9000px down) into the hero
Convert canada-visa-hero-banner.png (869KB, 94% wasted) and breadcrumb.png (421KB) to WebP

categories.name: Technical SEO
what_works: Apex 301-redirects to www; canonical host consistent
All pages carry correct self-referencing canonicals; 0 canonical mismatches across 15 inspected URLs
Correct 'index, follow' meta robots sitewide
Static HTML with full raw/rendered parity — no JS-rendering dependency
True 404 status codes; no mixed content; no duplicate titles or descriptions
Sitemap is valid XML, declared in robots.txt, returns 200
TTFB genuinely strong: 222ms with X-Vercel-Cache HIT

findings.title: Seven URLs are completely unknown to Google, including every commercial service page
findings.description: GSC URL Inspection returns coverage_state 'URL is unknown to Google' for /services/, /services/us-visa-appointment-canada/, /services/us-visa-appointment-toronto/, /about/, /terms/, /privacy/, /refund-policy/ — with page_fetch_state PAGE_FETCH_STATE_UNSPECIFIED, referring_urls [], and no last_crawl_time. Not crawled and rejected; never discovered at all. The 7 indexed URLs are the homepage, /how-it-works/, /contact/, /blog/, and the 3 blog posts. Cross-validated by two independent inspection runs with identical results.
findings.recommendation: Resubmit sitemap.xml in GSC, then use URL Inspection > Request Indexing on each of the 7. Do NOT use the Indexing API — it officially supports only JobPosting and BroadcastEvent. Do NOT add internal links as a fix: /services/ already has 8 homepage links while /blog/ is indexed with none, so linking is demonstrably not the cause.

findings.title: Service hub links to three pages that are simultaneously 404 and robots.txt-blocked
findings.description: /services/us-visa-appointment-{dubai,uae,australia}/ each return HTTP 404 and are each Disallow'd in robots.txt. All three are hard-linked from both /services/ and the homepage, and the /services/ meta description advertises them: 'We help applicants in Canada, Dubai, UAE, Australia and more.' Because robots.txt blocks crawling, Googlebot can never observe the 404, so the URLs cannot be cleanly dropped — Disallow is the wrong instrument for removing pages. Users clicking 'Dubai' from the service hub hit a dead end.
findings.recommendation: Choose one path per location. Building them: delete the three Disallow lines, ship at 200, add to sitemap (recommended for Dubai — a ranking Dubai blog post already exists to link into). Abandoning them: remove links from /services/ and homepage, delete the Disallow lines so Google can process removal, serve 410 Gone, and correct the /services/ meta description.

findings.title: Google is working from a stale 10-URL sitemap last processed 2026-06-23
findings.description: GSC Sitemaps API reports last_submitted 2026-06-23T04:30:36Z with contents [{type: web, submitted: 10}], while the live sitemap contains 14 URLs. Zero errors, zero warnings — Google simply has not re-fetched in roughly 7 weeks. Every URL carries the identical lastmod value 2026-08-07; uniform templated lastmod values are a known trigger for Google discounting the field entirely.
findings.recommendation: Resubmit sitemap.xml in GSC. Emit truthful per-page lastmod values, or omit lastmod entirely — omitting beats faking. Drop priority and changefreq, which Google ignores. If GSC still reports 10 URLs after 14 days, check for a stale edge-cached sitemap.xml on Vercel.

findings.title: Favicon 404s on 8 of 14 pages due to file-extension case mismatch
findings.description: brand-logo-real.PNG returns 200; brand-logo-real.png returns 404. Vercel static hosting is case-sensitive. Eight pages reference the lowercase path, and no /favicon.ico fallback exists.
findings.recommendation: Normalize the filename case across all references and add a /favicon.ico fallback.

findings.title: Security headers effectively absent
findings.description: The only security header present sitewide is Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=63072000 (lacking includeSubDomains and preload). Missing: Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy. These are not ranking factors, but this site handles passport details and payment intent in a scam-adjacent category.
findings.recommendation: Add via vercel.json: X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin, X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN, Permissions-Policy. Add CSP only after auditing gtag.js and analytics.ahrefs.com, and verify analytics still fires after deployment.

findings.title: /for-agents/ silently retired, losing the site's best-positioned page
findings.description: /for-agents -> 308 -> /for-agents/ -> 308 -> /services/ -> 200 (two hops). It still earns 6 impressions at average position 11.2, the best average position on the site, because GSC's last crawl (2026-06-24) predates the redirect. It was folded into /services/, a ~507-word consumer directory with zero B2B content — and /services/ is itself unindexed. Clicks from that stale result land on a broken destination.
findings.recommendation: Collapse the chain to a single hop. Separately, decide deliberately whether to reinstate a real B2B page — SERPs for agent/B2B queries show near-zero government competition and dedicated competitors already ranking.

categories.name: Content Quality
what_works: Per-page content quality scored 84-96/100 with zero filler or AI-slop pattern matches
Pricing honesty: 'no upfront fee', 'pay only on success'
Explicit 'we cannot guarantee a date' language — responsible for this category
Well-structured, anchor-linked refund policy
Substantial page depth: Toronto 3573 words, homepage 2968, Canada service 2795

findings.title: No verifiable legal entity, and /terms/ promises details it does not provide
findings.description: /terms/ states 'Our registered details are set out at the top of this page and on our About page,' but the content shows only 'Operated by: Easy Visa Booking' (a trading name) and a founder's personal name. No company number, registered address, or jurisdiction. A broken promise about registration details is worse than silence in a YMYL context.
findings.recommendation: Publish company registration number, registered address, and jurisdiction on both /terms/ and /about/.

findings.title: Zero testimonials, reviews, or third-party validation anywhere on the site
findings.description: Homepage HTML contains the literal comment '<!-- Testimonial section removed -->'. Claimed confirmation screenshots are described as 'available on request' rather than shown. In a scam-heavy niche this is the single largest conversion and trust gap.
findings.recommendation: Collect and publish real attributed client outcomes (name or initials, city, date, result). Show the confirmation screenshots. Do NOT add Review/AggregateRating schema until genuine on-page reviews exist — self-serve review markup violates Google policy.

findings.title: 65-75% verbatim duplication between the two location pages
findings.description: 75% of /services/us-visa-appointment-canada/ text appears verbatim in /services/us-visa-appointment-toronto/ (8-word shingle overlap coefficient 65.4%). Toronto is a city inside Canada, so the pages compete directly. This is the doorway-page pattern, and it is the template that would be replicated if location pages scale.
findings.recommendation: Either differentiate genuinely with consulate-specific wait times and local detail, or consolidate to one page. Quality gate before scaling: 60%+ unique content required at 30+ location pages; hard stop requiring justification at 50+.

findings.title: No author bylines or stated credentials on any blog post
findings.description: Zero genuine bylines across all three posts. For YMYL content explaining consulate and AIS mechanics, named authors with relevant stated experience are a direct Expertise signal.
findings.recommendation: Add named author bylines with relevant credentials and an author bio, plus matching Person schema.

findings.title: Three-way keyword cannibalization on the Canada appointment cluster
findings.description: The Canada blog guide and both service pages target the same term cluster. GSC shows the blog post absorbing all 300 impressions while the service pages get none — currently masked by the fact that the service pages are unindexed. Once indexation is fixed, the cannibalization becomes active.
findings.recommendation: Split intent explicitly before fixing indexation: informational content on the blog, transactional intent on the service page, with clear cross-links.

categories.name: On-Page SEO
what_works: Every page has a hand-written, specific meta description — a genuine strength
Descriptive, keyword-aligned title tags on all pages
H1 present on all analyzed pages
No duplicate titles or descriptions sitewide

findings.title: No og:description or twitter:card sitewide; homepage og:image returns 404
findings.description: Homepage has og:title, og:type, og:url, og:image — but og:image points to /img/visa-banner.jpg, which does not exist. No other page has og:image at all, and twitter:card is absent sitewide. The service is promoted via WhatsApp and Telegram, both advertised contact channels, where link previews are a direct acquisition surface.
findings.recommendation: Add og:description and twitter:card sitewide, fix the og:image path, and add per-page og:image.

findings.title: /services/ is thinner than its own child pages and cannot carry hub duty
findings.description: /services/ is ~507 words while its children are 2795 (Canada) and 3573 (Toronto). It also contains roughly 1200-1500px of dead space and an empty styled box between the location cards and the footer.
findings.recommendation: Rebuild /services/ as a genuine hub, or build a separate informational pillar and demote /services/ to a directory.

findings.title: /blog/ is unlinked from header nav and footer
findings.description: No navigational link to /blog/ exists anywhere on the site. It is indexed regardless, but receives no internal equity and users cannot discover it.
findings.recommendation: Add /blog/ to the primary navigation and footer.

findings.title: Meta descriptions exceed SERP render limit
findings.description: Lengths run 162-231 characters against a ~155-character safe limit. Toronto (216) and the Dubai blog post (231) lose their differentiating clauses ('Pay only on success') to truncation.
findings.recommendation: Front-load the differentiating value proposition within the first 155 characters.

findings.title: Three titles exceed 60 characters
findings.description: Toronto (72), homepage (65), Canada service (65).
findings.recommendation: Trim to under 60 characters, preserving the primary keyword and brand.

categories.name: Schema / Structured Data
what_works: All existing JSON-LD parses valid
No deprecated schema types in use
Dates are accurate ISO 8601
No fabricated reviews or ratings

findings.title: Unfilled placeholder text live in production schema
findings.description: Homepage Organization.sameAs contains the literal string 'https://t.me/YourTelegramChannel'. The real, live Telegram channel, confirmed in the footer HTML, is https://t.me/earlyusvisabooking.
findings.recommendation: Replace with the real URL. Ready-to-paste fix in findings/schema-generated/01-homepage-organization-website-service-graph.jsonld

findings.title: /contact/ ships zero JSON-LD
findings.description: The page most in need of machine-readable ContactPoint has no structured data at all, despite email, phone (+91-8849146234), and WhatsApp all being verified live on the page.
findings.recommendation: Add ContactPoint schema. Template in findings/schema-generated/05-contact-page.jsonld

findings.title: image property missing from all three BlogPosting blocks
findings.description: image is Google's most consistently required Article property for rich-result eligibility, and none of the three blog posts include it.
findings.recommendation: Add image to each BlogPosting. Template in findings/schema-generated/02-blogposting-template.jsonld

findings.title: No @id entity linking; Organization duplicated as 7+ anonymous islands
findings.description: The homepage declares Organization twice (top-level and nested inside Service.provider) with no @id. /about/, both service location pages, and all three blog posts (author and publisher each) add further disconnected stub copies. This fragments entity consolidation for Google and AI crawlers alike — and entity clarity is precisely what this site most needs.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a single @id-referenced Organization node and reference it everywhere. Pattern in findings/schema-generated/01, applied across files 04-07.

findings.title: BreadcrumbList absent on 6 pages; offers missing from both Service blocks
findings.description: BreadcrumbList is missing from /, /services/, /how-it-works/, /contact/, /blog/, and /for-agents/. Both /services/ location pages omit offers from their Service schema.
findings.recommendation: Templates in findings/schema-generated/03-breadcrumblist-missing-pages.jsonld and 04-service-location-pages-offers.jsonld

findings.title: Existing FAQPage blocks no longer produce a SERP feature
findings.description: Four FAQPage blocks exist (homepage, Toronto service page, 2 blog posts). Google retired FAQ rich results for ALL sites on 2026-05-07, so these no longer generate any SERP feature.
findings.recommendation: Leave them in place — they remain valid structured data and removal costs effort for no gain. Do not add new FAQPage markup expecting Google SERP benefit, and do not assume a confirmed AI-citation benefit. Use QAPage only for genuine user Q&A.

categories.name: Performance (CWV)
what_works: TTFB genuinely strong at 222ms with X-Vercel-Cache HIT — server response is not a bottleneck
Mobile CLS is 0 on all 5 tested pages
Desktop LCP passes on every page (1.3-2.0s)
Ahrefs analytics cost is negligible (3.7KB, ~4ms)

findings.title: CrUX field data unavailable — CWV is currently a weak ranking lever
findings.description: crux_history.py returned 404 'Insufficient Chrome traffic volume for eligibility', and every PageSpeed Insights response returned empty field_metrics. Consistent with 382 impressions over 90 days. Google's actual CWV ranking assessment uses 75th-percentile field data, which cannot be computed for this site. All metrics below are Lighthouse lab data.
findings.recommendation: Fix the image weight issues because they are cheap and genuinely bad, but do not prioritize CWV above indexation, trust, and link acquisition — it is not currently a functioning ranking signal for this domain.

findings.title: Unoptimized PNGs cause 7.2-11.7s mobile LCP
findings.description: canada-visa-hero-banner.png is 869KB (94% wasted bytes) and breadcrumb.png is 421KB (31% wasted). Zero WebP/AVIF adoption sitewide. Mobile LCP measures 7.2s-11.7s across the 5 tested pages (lab), against a 2.5s 'good' threshold.
findings.recommendation: Convert to WebP/AVIF and resize to displayed dimensions. This alone should move mobile LCP substantially.

findings.title: LCP image not preloaded or prioritized on any page
findings.description: The lcp-discovery-insight audit fails on every page; preload score is 50/100 and no image carries fetchpriority='high'.
findings.recommendation: Add fetchpriority='high' to the LCP image and preload it; avoid lazy-loading above-the-fold images.

findings.title: Desktop CLS 1.039 on homepage and 0.501 on blog
findings.description: Traced to a full-body-level shift, plausibly the full-viewport #spinner overlay. Against a 0.1 'good' threshold. Mobile CLS is 0, so this is desktop-specific.
findings.recommendation: Confirm in DevTools, then reserve space or remove the overlay. Add explicit width/height to all images — 100% currently lack them.

findings.title: gtag.js dominates third-party main-thread cost
findings.description: Up to 656ms main-thread time, including two long tasks of 400ms and 224ms on /services/ desktop. Render-blocking style.css costs 219ms, and FontAwesome causes FOIT (380ms + 235ms wasted) for a 170KB kit serving a small icon set.
findings.recommendation: Defer gtag.js, subset or replace FontAwesome with inline SVG icons, and inline critical CSS. Leave Ahrefs analytics alone — it is negligible.

categories.name: AI Search Readiness
what_works: All major AI crawlers unblocked: GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot, Claude-User, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Applebot-Extended, CCBot, meta-externalagent, Bingbot, Google-Extended
The /how-it-works/ 4-step process is genuinely well-formed, self-contained, citable content
The Canada guide's wait-time answer is source-attributed and extractable

findings.title: Homepage FAQ schema and visible FAQ accordion contain entirely different content
findings.description: The FAQPage JSON-LD carries 7 Q&As and the visible on-page accordion carries 6 — different questions and different answers. Critically, the only stated price ($100 starting fee) exists solely in the schema and never appears in visible text. Structured data must describe what is on the page.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the schema to mirror the visible FAQ exactly, and put the price in visible page copy.

findings.title: Entity signals are the weakest dimension — contradictory service-area claims
findings.description: The site states up to six different, mutually contradictory lists of which countries it serves, across Organization description, Organization areaServed, Service areaServed, About page schema, visible FAQ text, and a homepage subheading. Only Canada has an actual indexable location page. Compounded by the sameAs placeholder bug and no discoverable Wikipedia, Reddit, or review-platform presence.
findings.recommendation: Pick one authoritative service-area list matching pages that actually exist, and apply it consistently across schema and visible copy.

findings.title: Trust and authority, not formatting, are the binding constraint on AI citation
findings.description: With 9 clicks and average position 45.2 over 90 days, the domain is not in the candidate pool most AI answer engines draw from. This is a YMYL commercial-intermediary category with heavy scam activity, where AI engines are conservative about citing paid intermediaries.
findings.recommendation: Treat AI visibility as downstream of trust and authority work, not as a markup exercise. Formatting improvements alone will not produce citations here.

findings.title: llms.txt absent
findings.description: https://www.easyvisabooking.com/llms.txt returns 404. Stated honestly: llms.txt is not used by Google and no major AI vendor has confirmed production use.
findings.recommendation: Optional and cheap, but do not let it displace trust and authority work. Low backlog priority.

categories.name: Images
what_works: 100% alt-text coverage across all analyzed pages

findings.title: Large unoptimized PNGs with zero modern format adoption
findings.description: canada-visa-hero-banner.png 869KB (94% wasted), breadcrumb.png 421KB (31% wasted). No WebP or AVIF anywhere on the site.
findings.recommendation: Convert to WebP/AVIF, resize to displayed dimensions, and serve responsive srcset.

findings.title: 100% of images lack explicit width and height attributes
findings.description: Includes the hero carousel image, which is likely the LCP element. This is a direct layout-shift risk and correlates with the 1.039 desktop CLS on the homepage.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit width and height to every img element.

findings.title: Homepage og:image points to a 404
findings.description: /img/visa-banner.jpg does not exist under any tested name or case. No other page defines og:image at all.
findings.recommendation: Fix the path and add per-page social preview images.

categories.name: Visual / Mobile UX
what_works: Viewport meta correct; 16px base font
No intrusive interstitials — the full-viewport #spinner is visibility:hidden and opacity:0 post-load
Mobile hamburger menu functions correctly
100% alt-text coverage

findings.title: Government-affiliation disclaimer is buried in the footer
findings.description: The site has well-worded copy — 'We are not affiliated with... the U.S. Government' — but it sits in the global footer roughly 9,000px down the homepage, invisible without deliberate scrolling. In this category, that sentence is the first question every visitor has.
findings.recommendation: Move it into the hero, above the fold, on every page. Stating it prominently increases rather than decreases conversion here.

findings.title: No phone number anywhere despite schema and a trust badge promising phone support
findings.description: No tel: links exist site-wide; contact is email, WhatsApp, and Telegram only. Schema and a homepage trust badge both imply phone availability.
findings.recommendation: Either add a real phone number or remove the claim from schema and the trust badge.

findings.title: Confirmed mobile horizontal overflow
findings.description: 48px horizontal overflow on the homepage and 22px on /services/us-visa-appointment-canada/ at 390px width. Blog and contact pages are clean.
findings.recommendation: Identify the overflowing element and constrain with max-width: 100%.

findings.title: Fixed WhatsApp button overlaps body copy on mobile contact page
findings.description: The fixed-position WhatsApp button covers content on /contact/ at 390px width.
findings.recommendation: Add bottom padding to the content container, or reposition the button.

findings.title: Pricing never visible above the fold
findings.description: pricingMentioned is false on the homepage; the services page states only 'no upfront payment' with no figures anywhere.
findings.recommendation: Surface the pay-on-success model and the starting fee above the fold — it is a competitive advantage currently hidden.

categories.name: Backlinks / Authority
categories.score_note: No numeric score reported — insufficient data. Backlink Tier 0 (Common Crawl + verification crawler only); Moz and Bing Webmaster keys unconfigured. Only 1 of 7 scoring factors has any data source, so a score would be fabrication.
what_works: Domain is present in Common Crawl's Jan-Mar 2026 web graph and clears its ranking threshold

findings.title: Link acquisition is very likely the binding constraint on the entire site
findings.description: The domain sits at the bottom of the Common Crawl authority distribution (PageRank rank ~1.2M, harmonic centrality rank ~377K; confidence 0.50). No candidate backlink URLs surfaced anywhere in this audit. Cross-referenced against GSC positions of 45-80 on commercial head terms with real impression volume, this supports a blunt conclusion: without referring domains, the site will not rank for competitive commercial terms regardless of on-page quality.
findings.recommendation: Start a standing link-acquisition workstream. Highest leverage: digital PR around proprietary visa wait-time data that no government portal publishes. Then university international-student offices, immigration and expat community resources, HR/global-mobility publications. Explicitly avoid PBNs, paid link networks, mass guest posting, and comment/forum spam — elevated penalty risk in this niche.

findings.title: Backlink measurement is currently blind
findings.description: Referring domain count, anchor text distribution, toxic ratio, link velocity, and follow/nofollow ratio are all unavailable at Tier 0.
findings.recommendation: Configure the free Moz API tier (2,500 rows/month, https://moz.com/products/api) — the only free source returning referring-domain count and spam score. Add moz_api_key to ~/.config/claude-seo/backlinks-api.json. Then Bing Webmaster Tools (free, https://www.bing.com/webmasters), which also feeds Microsoft Copilot citations.

categories.name: Search Experience (SXO)
what_works: Genuine trust strengths: explicit non-affiliation disclaimer, pay-on-success pricing, well-structured anchor-linked refund policy
Content matches query intent where it targets the right queries

findings.title: Broad commercial queries are structurally unwinnable
findings.description: Live SERP checks confirm 'canada us visa appointment'-class queries are owned by ais.usvisa-info.com (the official booking portal itself), travel.state.gov, and ca.usembassy.gov. No commercial content page displaces a government portal on those terms. Head terms return SERPs 40-70% dominated by government domains plus funded incumbents (Atlys, VisaGrader, CheckVisaSlots).
findings.recommendation: Redirect strategy to the adjacent winnable cluster — rescheduling mechanics, slot-release timing, service legitimacy, and cost transparency — where SERPs are blog- and forum-dominated with near-zero government presence.

findings.title: The flagship page's zero CTR is a position problem, not a snippet problem
findings.description: /blog/us-visa-appointment-canada-guide-2026/ has 300 impressions, 0 clicks, average position 50.3. Expected clicks at position 50 from 300 impressions is under 1, so zero is statistically unsurprising. The page is 2745 words, well-structured, scored 84/100 on content quality, and its queries map cleanly onto its content. Period-over-period, impressions nearly tripled (64 to 236) across long-tail Canada queries but all sit at position 41-97 — which is why sitewide CTR fell from 3.26% to 1.47% while impressions rose 196%.
findings.recommendation: Do NOT rewrite the title or meta description — that optimizes the wrong variable. The fix is authority-building plus retargeting to the winnable query cluster.

findings.title: Apparent striking-distance positions are statistical noise
findings.description: /services/ at position 1.0, /how-it-works/ at 4.0, /blog/ at 5.0, and /for-agents/ at 11.2 are each built from 1-4 total impressions, never appear in the query-by-page breakdown (queries fall below GSC's anonymization threshold), and are non-persistent — /services/'s position 1.0 appeared once in the prior 28-day window and vanished in the latest. /services/ is not even indexed.
findings.recommendation: Do not treat these as quick wins. Optimizing them would target noise.

findings.title: B2B persona scores 15/100 with no page to land on
findings.description: /for-agents/ 308-redirects to /services/, a 507-word consumer location directory with zero mention of agents, B2B, or bulk booking — while GSC still shows 6 impressions at position 11.2 landing there. SERP data for agent/B2B queries shows near-zero government competition and dedicated competitors already ranking (usvisaagents.com, path2usa.com, giecglobal.com).
findings.recommendation: Reinstate a dedicated B2B page in the sitemap with a persistent nav link, or consciously drop the audience. Currently it is being lost by accident.
